You review the "What's new" notes that Ion Studio will show to every person who uses it, the first time it opens after an update. A note reaches them only if you keep it.

Below are the changes that went into this release, written by engineers, and then the proposed notes, numbered.

Judge each note on its own. Keep a note only if it passes every check:

1. Accurate: it describes something the changes actually do. Nothing invented, exaggerated, or promised.
2. Plain: an everyday person who has never seen the code understands it on one quick read. No technical terms, code, file names, abbreviations, or names of internal parts of the system. Words an everyday computer user knows (account, sign in, update, download, folder, window, tab, search) are plain, and so are the names of features exactly as Ion Studio shows them on screen (Settings, Inbox, Fleet).
3. Appropriate for everyone: professional and neutral. Nothing rude, offensive, sarcastic, joking, political, or alarming. No security details of any kind.
4. Makes sense on its own: a complete, clear sentence that does not depend on knowing the other notes or the changes.

When unsure, drop the note.

Answer with one line per note, in order, and nothing else:

1: KEEP
2: DROP <the check it failed, in a few words>
